required_outcomes: Records the landlord's written approval (24 May) of Harbour's £285 inc VAT quote as the basis for the spend.
Approves the quote or instructs Harbour Services to order the parts and complete the repair for no more than £285, and asks them to book the visit with the tenant.
Tells the tenant the repair is approved, that parts take 3 to 5 working days and that Harbour will contact them to book, without inventing a date.
Confirms to the landlord that the repair has been instructed.
acceptable_alternatives: Also asking Harbour for the oven's make, model and serial number so the landlord can try a manufacturer claim later, provided the repair is not held up.
Holding the case awaiting Harbour's booking after instructing them, with a follow-up date.
positive_behaviours: Keeps the manufacturer warranty as an optional later claim, as the landlord said.
Records Harbour's parts lead time on the case.
red_flags: Escalating to a human, or holding for the landlord again, when he has clearly decided.
Pursuing the manufacturer warranty first against the landlord's instruction.
prohibited_actions: Approving more than £285, or work beyond the heating element and fan motor.
critical_failures: Leaving the repair uninstructed (re-asking the landlord, holding for the warranty check or escalating) after the landlord's explicit approval of the £285.
